summary: Without task container limits, controller capacity on OpenShift comes from the node's CPU and memory seen by the pod, which can overload a shared node. Instead of hard limits you can set SYSTEM_TASK_ABS_MEM (for example 3gi) and SYSTEM_TASK_ABS_CPU (750m) through extra_settings as a soft in-application limit that avoids CPU throttling and OOM reaping.
questions: How do I limit controller capacity without setting pod limits?
Why does controller think it has the whole node's capacity on OpenShift?

answer_card.title: Soft-limit controller capacity with extra_settings
answer_card.answer_md:
If you do not set limits on the task container, capacity is calculated from the underlying node's CPU and memory, which can overload a shared node. Set a soft limit instead through `extra_settings`:

```
SYSTEM_TASK_ABS_MEM = 3gi
SYSTEM_TASK_ABS_CPU = 750m
```

Controller then limits how much work it starts, without Kubernetes CPU throttling or OOM reaping. Values use the Kubernetes resource format.
